name: Citibank Cash Management system fraud (Vladimir Levin)
vector: Compromised customer credentials for dial-up corporate cash-management service (how obtained remains debated)
sequence: Logged into Citicorp's corporate cash-management system as corporate customers; issued ~40 transfer instructions to accounts in Finland, US, Netherlands, Germany, Israel; mules attempted withdrawals.
regulatory: Citibank introduced smart-card/token authentication for the service (reported)
legal: Levin arrested London (Stansted) Mar 1995, extradited 1997, pleaded guilty 1998, sentenced to 3 years
root_causes: Static password authentication for high-value remote payment initiation
worked: Bank monitoring of anomalous transfers; international law-enforcement cooperation
lessons: High-value remote payment initiation requires strong authentication; first widely reported 'online bank robbery'.
unresolved: How credentials were obtained (later claims that another hacker sold access are unverified)

name: CardSystems Solutions processor breach
vector: SQL injection into processor web application (per FTC complaint)
sequence: Attacker installed scripts that harvested stored track data, which processor retained in violation of card-network rules.
downtime: Processor lost Visa/Amex acceptance; acquired by Pay By Touch
regulatory: FTC consent order (2006); accelerated PCI DSS adoption
root_causes: Storing prohibited data; insecure web application
lessons: Processors are concentration points for card risk; PCI DSS (2004) became enforced in practice.

name: Estonia cyber disruptions (incl. Hansabank / SEB online banking)
org: Estonian government, media and banks (Hansabank, SEB Eesti Ühispank)
attacker: Pro-Russian activists; botnets. Russian state involvement alleged, never officially proven
attribution: Low for state; one Estonian national convicted
vector: Volumetric DDoS via botnets, coordinated on Russian-language forums
sequence: Waves of DDoS after relocation of Soviet war memorial (Bronze Soldier); peak 9 May. Banks restricted foreign traffic to keep domestic service.
systems: Internet banking front-ends, DNS, government sites
downtime: Hansabank online banking unavailable ~1.5 hours on 10 May; foreign access blocked for longer (reported)
regulatory: Prompted NATO CCDCOE (Tallinn, 2008) and national cyber doctrine
fs_impact: Hansabank cited losses of ~EUR 1m (reported, low confidence)
root_causes: Highly digitised society with limited DDoS mitigation capacity
worked: Geo-filtering preserved domestic access; CERT-EE coordination
lessons: DDoS can be a geopolitical instrument; banks are symbolic national targets.

name: Heartland Payment Systems breach
vector: SQL injection, then sniffer malware on processing network
sequence: Entry via web app, lateral movement to payment network, packet sniffers captured unencrypted track data in transit.
downtime: Removed from Visa compliant list temporarily
regulatory: Encryption-in-transit / end-to-end encryption push in PCI ecosystem
fs_impact: Heartland reported charges of ~USD 140m (company filings, reported)
root_causes: Unencrypted card data in transit internally
lessons: PCI compliance status did not prevent breach - an early 'compliance is not security' case.

name: RBS WorldPay payroll-card ATM cash-out
vector: Network intrusion into processor; decrypted PINs for payroll cards
sequence: Raised withdrawal limits on 44 payroll debit cards, cloned cards distributed to cashers; >2,100 ATMs hit in ~12 hours.
regulatory: Template for later 'Unlimited Operations' warnings
root_causes: Compromise of card-management system allowing limit changes
lessons: Altering authorization parameters is more lucrative than stealing data.

name: Zeus banking trojan cash-out network (Operation Trident Breach)
attribution: High for mules (arrests); medium for developers
vector: Phishing emails installing Zeus on SME treasury PCs
sequence: Man-in-the-browser web injects captured credentials/OTPs; fraudulent ACH/wire transfers to mule accounts.
regulatory: FFIEC Supplement to Authentication in an Internet Banking Environment (June 2011)
fs_impact: Losses often borne by SMEs; litigation (e.g., Patco v. Ocean Bank)
lessons: The customer endpoint is part of the bank's attack surface.
unresolved: Core Zeus developer later charged (Bogachev, 2014) remains at large

name: Citigroup credit-card online account breach
vector: Web application flaw: after login, changing account number in URL exposed other accounts (widely reported)
sequence: Automated enumeration of account identifiers retrieved names, account numbers, contact info.
stolen_orig: ~USD 2.7m fraud losses (reported by media from Citi statements)
regulatory: Congressional letters; contributed to FFIEC focus
lessons: Even top-tier card issuers' customer portals are exposed to simple authorization logic flaws.

name: Fidelity National Information Services prepaid card cash-out
sequence: See sources
lessons: Processor limit manipulation again.

name: Operation Ababil DDoS on US banks
org: ~46 US financial institutions (JPMorgan, BofA, Wells Fargo, NYSE, Nasdaq among them)
attacker: ITSec Team and Mersad Co., working on behalf of Iran's IRGC (per DOJ indictment)
sequence: 176 days of DDoS; peak traffic ~140 Gbps (DOJ); 'Izz ad-Din al-Qassam Cyber Fighters' persona.
downtime: Intermittent hours of outage across banks
customers: Hundreds of thousands unable to access accounts (DOJ)
regulatory: FFIEC joint statement on DDoS (Apr 2014)
lessons: State actors use banks for coercive signalling; availability is a core banking control objective.

name: 'Unlimited Operations' prepaid card cash-outs (RAKBANK, Bank Muscat)
org: RAKBANK; Bank Muscat (via card processors in India and US)
attacker: Transnational ring; New York cell charged
sequence: Removed withdrawal limits on prepaid debit cards, distributed card data; ~40,500 withdrawals in ~10 hours on 19 Feb 2013.
regulatory: FFIEC 'Cyber-attacks on financial institutions' ATM Unlimited Cash-Out alert (Apr 2014)
root_causes: Third-party processors with authority to change limits
lessons: Third-party processors can be the weakest link in card authorization.

name: DarkSeoul wiper attack on South Korean banks and broadcasters
org: Shinhan Bank, NongHyup, Jeju Bank; KBS, MBC, YTN
attacker: North Korea (RGB-linked) per South Korean government
vector: Compromised patch-management servers used to push wiper (reported)
sequence: Wiper overwrote MBRs on ~32,000+ PCs and servers at 14:00 local; ATMs and online banking affected.
downtime: Hours to days at affected banks
customers: Millions of customers affected by service interruption
regulatory: Korean FSC strengthened IT security (network separation) rules
root_causes: Centralised IT management tools turned into distribution channel
lessons: Destructive attacks against banks are a geopolitical tool; admin tooling is a high-value target.

name: Target card-data breach (retailer, card ecosystem)
org: Target Corp. (card-issuing banks bore reissuance costs)
vector: Stolen credentials of HVAC vendor; POS RAM-scraping malware
sequence: Vendor access -> network pivot -> POS malware -> exfiltration of ~40m card numbers and 70m customer records.
regulatory: Accelerated US EMV chip migration (Oct 2015 liability shift)
fs_impact: Target reported >USD 200m net costs; settlements with card issuers (reported)
lessons: Card-issuing banks bear losses for breaches outside their perimeter.

name: Carbanak / Anunak bank intrusions
sequence: Long dwell; studied internal procedures via screen capture; inflated balances, instructed ATMs to dispense, moved funds via e-payment systems.
systems: Internal banking systems, ATM control, payment systems
stolen_orig: Up to USD 1bn claimed (Kaspersky estimate; not independently verified)
regulatory: Europol/EC3 joint investigation
root_causes: Phishing + long dwell + weak internal monitoring
lessons: Attackers learn and imitate legitimate bank operator workflows - signature detection fails.
unresolved: Total loss figure is a security-vendor estimate

name: JPMorgan Chase data breach
attacker: Gery Shalon, Ziv Orenstein, Joshua Aaron et al. (criminal enterprise)
motive: Financial (securities pump-and-dump marketing, illegal gambling, payment processing)
vector: Stolen employee credentials on a server that lacked two-factor authentication (widely reported)
sequence: Access to contact databases and ~90 servers; contact data used for stock-promotion schemes.
process: None directly (no account credentials/funds taken per JPM)
customers: 76m households and 7m small businesses (contact info) per 8-K
regulatory: Heightened FFIEC/NYDFS attention; influenced NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500 (2017) MFA emphasis
fs_impact: JPM stated plan to spend ~USD 250m/yr on cyber (pre-existing)
lessons: A single unprotected server can expose a top-tier bank; data theft can fund market manipulation.

name: Banco del Austro SWIFT fraud
sequence: ~12 fraudulent SWIFT messages via Wells Fargo correspondent over 10 days.
regulatory: Became known after Bangladesh case
root_causes: Credential compromise at local SWIFT endpoint
lessons: Precursor to Bangladesh Bank: correspondent banks process authenticated messages as genuine.

name: Tien Phong Bank SWIFT attempt
sequence: See sources
lessons: Third-party SWIFT software (PDF reader) targeted.

name: Bangladesh Bank / Federal Reserve Bank of New York SWIFT heist
attacker: Lazarus Group / North Korea (DOJ complaint vs Park Jin Hyok, 2018)
attribution: High (US criminal complaint; consistent with vendor forensics)
vector: Spear-phishing emails to Bangladesh Bank staff (FBI complaint)
sequence: Initial access traced to phishing from early 2015 (FBI complaint); months of dwell; malware on SWIFT Alliance Access server manipulated the local database and suppressed printed confirmations; 35 payment orders (~USD 951m) sent to the NY Fed on a Thursday night/Friday, timed around Bangladesh weekend and Philippine holiday.
systems: Bank's local SWIFT Alliance Access environment and printer (NOT SWIFT's central network)
process: Central-bank reserve account payments via correspondent
stolen_orig: USD 101m executed (81m to RCBC Philippines; 20m to Sri Lanka reversed)
settlement: 30 instructions held by NY Fed for review; one Sri Lanka payment stopped by name misspelling ('fandation')
regulatory: SWIFT Customer Security Programme (May 2016) and mandatory CSCF attestation (from 2017); NY Fed strengthened screening
fs_impact: Loss to Bangladesh Bank reserves; Governor resigned Mar 2016
legal: Philippine BSP fined RCBC PHP 1bn (2016); RCBC branch manager convicted 2019; Bangladesh Bank civil suits vs RCBC (US courts)
root_causes: Weak segregation and security of local SWIFT environment; reliance on paper confirmations; timing exploitation
failed: Network segmentation; integrity monitoring; daily reconciliation
worked: NY Fed sanctions/name screening on many instructions; Deutsche Bank/Pan Asia Bank queried misspelling
lessons: Attacker who controls a trusted message endpoint can 'speak with the bank's voice'. Message authentication != transaction legitimacy.
unresolved: Exact recovered total (publicly cited ~USD 15-18m from Philippines); full insider question in Bangladesh

name: Tesco Bank debit-card fraud attack
vector: Exploitation of predictable card number (PAN) generation and weaknesses in debit-card design (FCA final notice)
sequence: Generated valid card details; contactless/mag-stripe-type transactions over a weekend.
downtime: Online transactions suspended for debit customers
regulatory: FCA fine GBP 16.4m (Oct 2018) under Principle 2 (due skill, care and diligence)
root_causes: Card design and fraud-rule deficiencies; slow response
lessons: Regulators can penalise for failure to respond, not just failure to prevent.

name: Union Bank of India SWIFT attempt
attacker: Unknown (methods similar to Bangladesh case per reports)
sequence: ~USD 171m fraudulent SWIFT instructions; funds stopped/recovered.
regulatory: RBI SWIFT-related circulars (2016-2018)
lessons: Rapid reconciliation enables recall.

name: Equifax breach (credit bureau)
sequence: Dispute portal exploited; ~9,000 queries over 76 days; expired TLS certificate blinded inspection.
regulatory: FTC/CFPB/states settlement up to ~USD 700m (2019)
lessons: Credit-underwriting infrastructure is a national-security dataset.

name: NotPetya destructive malware (Ukrainian banks, central bank)
org: National Bank of Ukraine, Oschadbank and other Ukrainian banks
attacker: Russian GRU (Sandworm) per UK, US and other governments (Feb 2018)
vector: Trojanised update of M.E.Doc accounting software
sequence: Self-propagating wiper masquerading as ransomware.
systems: Windows estates incl. branch systems, ATMs
settlement: NBU reported payments disruption at some banks
regulatory: NBU cyber rules; global awareness of supply-chain wipers
lessons: Collateral damage can hit banks without being targeted directly.

name: Far Eastern International Bank SWIFT heist
sequence: ~USD 60m fraudulent SWIFT transfers to Sri Lanka, Cambodia, US; Hermes ransomware as distraction (reported).
regulatory: Taiwan FSC review
lessons: Post-CSP, attacks continued but recall improved.

name: Mexico SPEI third-party connection fraud
org: Several Mexican banks (e.g., Banorte) via SPEI connection software
vector: Compromise of participant-side connection applications to Banxico's SPEI
sequence: Fraudulent SPEI orders to mule accounts, cashed out at branches.
downtime: Participants moved to backup/contingency connection; slower payments
regulatory: Banxico new cyber rules for SPEI participants; CISO unit
lessons: Payment-system participant endpoints are FMI risk.

name: Banco de Chile wiper + SWIFT fraud
sequence: Wiper rendered ~9,000 workstations and ~500 servers unbootable; during the chaos, ~USD 10m sent via SWIFT to Hong Kong.
customers: Branch/office customers inconvenienced; no customer funds lost (bank)
regulatory: Chilean CMF cyber reporting rules (2018)
failed: Separating disruption response from payment monitoring
lessons: Destructive attacks can be cover for theft.

name: Cosmos Co-operative Bank ATM switch & SWIFT fraud
attacker: Unknown; FASTCash-style TTPs linked by US-CERT/vendors to Lazarus
category: ATM switch / card authorization manipulation + SWIFT
vector: Malware in bank environment; proxy switch inserted between bank's ATM switch and core banking (reported)
sequence: 11 Aug: proxy switch approved withdrawals from cloned Visa/RuPay cards without core-banking check: ~14,800 transactions abroad (~INR 78 crore) and ~2,800 domestic RuPay (~INR 2.5 crore). 13 Aug: 3 SWIFT transfers ~INR 13.9 crore to Hang Seng Bank (Hong Kong).
downtime: Card and online services suspended days
regulatory: RBI advisories; US-CERT FASTCash alert TA18-275A (Oct 2018)
root_causes: Authorization decision moved outside core-banking control
failed: Switch integrity; stand-in rules; velocity limits
lessons: Whoever controls the 'approve/decline' answer controls the money.

name: City Union Bank SWIFT fraud
sequence: See sources
lessons: Indian bank SWIFT controls tightened by RBI.

name: Capital One cloud data breach
vector: Misconfigured web application firewall enabling server-side request forgery to obtain cloud role credentials
sequence: Credentials used to list and copy S3 buckets with credit-card application data; attacker boasted online; tip via responsible-disclosure email.
systems: Cloud storage of credit-card application data
stolen_orig: No evidence data used for fraud (bank)
customers: ~100m US, ~6m Canada; ~140k SSNs, ~80k bank account numbers
regulatory: OCC civil money penalty USD 80m (Aug 2020) and consent order on risk management
fs_impact: Incremental costs ~USD 100-150m (company estimate 2019); USD 190m class settlement
legal: Thompson convicted (wire fraud, unauthorized access) June 2022
lessons: Cloud shifts risk to configuration and identity; card acquisition data is high-value.

name: First American Financial document exposure
sequence: See sources
lessons: NYDFS's first Part 500 enforcement; SEC disclosure-controls case.

name: SolarWinds Orion supply-chain compromise
org: ~18,000 Orion customers incl. financial institutions and US Treasury
sequence: Backdoor in signed update; selective second-stage intrusions.
regulatory: US EO 14028 (May 2021); software supply-chain focus
legal: SEC action vs SolarWinds (2023; largely dismissed 2024)
lessons: Trusted vendor updates are a systemic channel.
unresolved: Full scope of financial-sector second-stage access

name: New Zealand Exchange DDoS
sequence: Trading halted on four consecutive days.
regulatory: FMA review; NZX remediation
root_causes: Market-announcement dependency on single network path
lessons: Continuous disclosure obligations create DDoS fragility for exchanges.

name: Accellion FTA exploitation (Flagstar Bank, RBNZ and others)
org: Flagstar Bank; Reserve Bank of New Zealand; others
sequence: Data theft followed by extortion.
regulatory: RBNZ independent review (KPMG)
lessons: File-transfer tools are repeated mass-exploitation targets (later MOVEit, GoAnywhere).

name: Robinhood social-engineering data breach
sequence: See sources
lessons: Phone social engineering of support staff.

name: DDoS on Ukrainian banks (PrivatBank, Oschadbank) before invasion
attacker: Russian GRU (US and UK government attribution, 18 Feb 2022)
sequence: Online banking and apps degraded; SMS spam claiming ATM outages.
lessons: Cyber disruption of banks as pre-kinetic signalling and panic induction.

name: Ronin bridge theft (crypto)
sequence: See sources
lessons: DPRK theft migrates from banks to crypto; OFAC sanctioned Tornado Cash Aug 2022.

name: ION Trading Technologies (ION Cleared Derivatives) ransomware
sequence: Encryption of derivatives clearing middle-office platform used by ~42 clients (reported).
settlement: CFTC delayed Commitments of Traders reports
regulatory: CFTC statements; vendor concentration debate
lessons: A single middle-office vendor can impair market data used by the regulator.

name: MOVEit Transfer mass exploitation
org: Hundreds of orgs incl. banks, brokers, insurers
sequence: Mass data theft via file transfer servers then extortion listings.
customers: Tens of millions of individuals across sectors
regulatory: SEC/state notifications
root_causes: Zero-day in widely used vendor product
lessons: Fourth-party exposure: banks affected via their vendors' vendors.

name: Mr. Cooper mortgage servicer ransomware
sequence: Systems shut down; customers could not make payments online for ~a week; late fees waived.
regulatory: CFPB/state attention
worked: Late-fee waivers; no credit reporting of delayed payments
lessons: Servicing outages create technical delinquency that is not credit deterioration (see Part 7).

name: ICBC Financial Services ransomware (US broker-dealer)
org: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Financial Services LLC (ICBCFS)
vector: Not officially disclosed (Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966 widely suspected in reporting)
sequence: Ransomware encrypted systems at the US securities-clearing subsidiary; firm disconnected; unable to settle US Treasury and repo trades on behalf of clients; settlement info reportedly carried by USB/messenger; BNY Mellon exposure reported ~USD 9bn.
process: US Treasury / repo clearing via FICC
stolen_orig: N/A (ransom reportedly paid per LockBit claim; unconfirmed)
settlement: Some Treasury trades unsettled; SIFMA rerouted; parent reportedly injected capital
regulatory: SEC settled order (reported Dec 2024): recordkeeping violations, censure, no penalty, cited inadequate incident preparation
lessons: Operational failure at a small node can create settlement risk in the deepest market; parent support contained it.

name: Fidelity National Financial ransomware
sequence: See sources
lessons: Mortgage-closing pipeline disruption; early SEC Item 1.05 filer.

name: OCC email system compromise (regulator)
org: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
sequence: Access to ~100 officials' mailboxes containing sensitive supervisory information.
regulatory: Notified Congress as major incident
lessons: Supervisors hold bank vulnerability data - a target in itself.

name: EquiLend securities-lending platform ransomware
sequence: Trading and post-trade services offline; clients reverted to manual processes.
lessons: Market-structure utilities are ransomware targets.

name: Santander third-party database breach (Snowflake campaign)
vector: Stolen credentials to customer accounts on cloud data platform lacking MFA (Mandiant campaign)
sequence: Data exfiltrated from third-party-hosted database; offered for sale.
customers: Customers in Chile, Spain, Uruguay; staff
root_causes: No MFA on SaaS accounts; infostealer credentials
lessons: SaaS identity is a shared-responsibility gap.

name: DMM Bitcoin theft (crypto, Japan)
attacker: TraderTraitor / North Korea (FBI, NPA, DC3 joint statement Dec 2024)
vector: Social engineering of employee at wallet software vendor Ginco (per joint statement)
sequence: Manipulated legitimate transaction request; 4,502.9 BTC drained.
customers: Customers made whole via group funding
regulatory: FSA business improvement order
fs_impact: Exchange closed; accounts transferred to SBI VC Trade
lessons: Crypto custody is now a bank-adjacent theft channel for DPRK.

name: Evolve Bank & Trust ransomware (BaaS sponsor bank)
sequence: Data exfiltration; data posted; fintech partners notified customers.
regulatory: Separate Fed enforcement action (June 2024) on BaaS risk management
lessons: Small sponsor banks hold data of many fintech customers - hidden concentration.

name: Patelco Credit Union ransomware
sequence: Core and online banking shut down ~2 weeks; branches with limited services.
systems: Online banking, transfers, Zelle, account balances
customers: ~502k members lost services; ~726k individuals notified of data breach
regulatory: NCUA (72-hour reporting rule in force since Sep 2023)
lessons: Prolonged outage at a mid-size deposit institution did not trigger a run - but did trigger customer attrition and litigation.

name: CrowdStrike Falcon faulty update (NON-CYBERATTACK comparator)
org: ~8.5m Windows devices incl. banks, exchanges (e.g., LSEG RNS)
sequence: Kernel driver crash (BSOD) on boot.
regulatory: Fuelled DORA/critical third-party oversight debates
lessons: Concentration risk is realised without any attacker; resilience must be cause-agnostic.

name: C-Edge Technologies ransomware (Indian co-operative banks)
org: C-Edge Technologies (TCS-SBI JV) serving ~300 co-operative and regional rural banks
vector: Reported misconfigured Jenkins server at a related service provider (vendor research; not officially confirmed)
sequence: Ransomware hit C-Edge systems; NPCI temporarily isolated C-Edge from retail payment systems (UPI, IMPS, AePS, NFS ATM); member banks' customers could not transact.
customers: Customers of ~300 small banks (≈0.5% of national payment volume per NPCI)
settlement: Isolation prevented spread to NPCI network
regulatory: RBI/NPCI audits; CERT-In coordination
root_causes: Shared service-provider concentration for small banks
worked: NPCI isolation; staged reconnection after audit
lessons: Vendor compromise ≠ bank compromise, but customers experience it identically; isolation is a crucial circuit breaker.

name: Coinbase insider-bribery customer data theft
attacker: Criminal group bribing outsourced support agents
sequence: Agents exported customer data; data used for impersonation scams; USD 20m ransom refused.
stolen_orig: Customer scam losses; company estimated USD 180-400m remediation
regulatory: SEC 8-K
lessons: Insider access via BPO is a scalable attack path.

name: Bybit Ethereum cold-wallet theft
vector: Compromise of a developer machine at multisig wallet provider (Safe{Wallet}); malicious JavaScript altered signing UI
sequence: Signers approved a transaction that changed wallet logic; ~401k ETH drained; rapid laundering via swaps/bridges.
lessons: Largest single theft recorded; shows 'what you see is what you sign' failure.

name: Japan securities account takeovers and unauthorized trading
org: Multiple brokers (Rakuten Securities, Nomura, SBI Securities and others)
attacker: Unknown; phishing infrastructure; some reporting points to Chinese-speaking groups (unconfirmed)
sequence: Compromised accounts sold holdings and bought thinly traded (often Chinese small-cap) stocks to manipulate prices.
stolen_orig: Unauthorized sales JPY ~571bn (through June 2025, FSA reported)
customers: Thousands of accounts (3,312 initially; ~5,000 in April)
regulatory: FSA; JSDA mandatory phishing-resistant MFA/passkeys for logins and trades
lessons: Account-takeover at scale can be market abuse, not just theft.

name: Bank Sepah disruption and Nobitex destruction (Iran)
attacker: 'Predatory Sparrow' (Gonjeshke Darande) - claimed; widely linked by media to Israel (not officially confirmed)
sequence: Bank Sepah services disrupted; ~USD 90m of Nobitex crypto sent to unspendable 'burn' addresses.
lessons: Value destruction (not theft) as a war aim against financial institutions.

name: Lotte Card online payment system hack
vector: Web server vulnerability in online payment system (reported)
sequence: Log files containing personal credit information exfiltrated.
regulatory: FSC: 1.5-month new-card issuance suspension (Aug 1-Sep 15 2026) and fine (~KRW 5bn reported); PIPC fine KRW 9.62bn
lessons: First Korean business suspension for a hack - regulators escalating to franchise penalties.

name: CoinDCX hot-wallet theft (India)
sequence: See sources
lessons: Indian crypto-bank linkages.

name: FICOBA national bank-account registry intrusion (France)
org: French Ministry of Economy (DGFiP) - FICOBA registry
vector: Stolen credentials of a civil servant
sequence: Several days' access to registry entries.
customers: ~1.2m accounts (IBAN, identity, address, some tax IDs)
regulatory: CNIL notification
lessons: IBAN + identity data fuels SEPA direct-debit and impersonation fraud against banks' customers.

name: Citizens Financial & Frost Bank data exposure via statement/tax-document vendor
org: Citizens Financial Group; Frost Bank (vendor reportedly Sefas)
vector: Vendor SFTP server (per Frost-related filing as reported)
sequence: Data theft at print/fulfilment vendor; leak-site listing.
customers: Frost ~200k individuals (filing); Citizens 'limited' (bank); attacker claims 3.4m records
regulatory: State AG notifications
lessons: Low-glamour vendors (print, mail) aggregate bank customer PII.
unresolved: Vendor identity confirmed only in secondary sources

name: Iranian state banks card-system cyberattacks (ISC)
org: Bank Melli, Bank Saderat, Bank Tejarat, EDBI (via Informatics Services Corporation)
attacker: 'Black Wolves' claimed earlier attack; June 23 attack unattributed
sequence: Shared communications infrastructure attacked; ISC suspended card operations (ATM, POS, mobile) at three banks.
customers: National card-payment users of the banks
lessons: Shared national processors are single points of failure in conflict.

name: Payment/disbursement-API abuse against Indian NBFCs and fintechs (CERT-In CIAD-2026-0046)
org: Multiple NBFCs / digital lenders and their partner banks (e.g., Hyderabad NBFC; Unifinz Capital reported)
attacker: Unknown; CERT-In later linked activity to 'CRAFTY FALCON' (see INC-2026-007) per press
vector: Stolen API credentials of payment gateways/aggregators/partner-bank APIs (CERT-In, as reported)
sequence: Attackers invoked fund-transfer/disbursement APIs directly, generating rapid bursts of payouts to mule accounts. Reported cases: Hyderabad NBFC INR 3.3 crore in 87 minutes (19 Oct); reports of two Mumbai NBFCs losing ~USD 2m via >700 transfers on 8-9 Oct (single secondary source, unverified).
systems: NBFC disbursement systems and bank APIs
stolen_orig: Case-level: INR 3.3 crore (Hyderabad, REPORTED); aggregate ~INR 300 crore over two months (single outlet, UNVERIFIED)
settlement: Partner banks executed API instructions as authenticated
regulatory: RBI advisory 19 Oct 2026; RBI supervisory data requests (Reuters, 30 Oct 2026)
legal: Police complaints; arrests in related mule networks (not linked conclusively)
root_causes: Static API keys; no transaction-level anomaly limits; weak partner onboarding
worked: Partial freezing (e.g., INR 40 lakh of 3.3 crore)
lessons: API keys are the new SWIFT credentials: authenticated ≠ legitimate.
unresolved: Aggregate losses; victims; links between cases
verification: web-verified 2026-11-07 (press only; advisory text not retrieved)

name: State Bank of India customer data leak
sequence: Records surfaced on dark web; SBI alerted by threat-intel vendor, Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In.
regulatory: Exchange disclosure; RBI scrutiny
lessons: Disclosure gap between investors and data subjects criticised (IFF).

name: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa fraudulent transfers via service-provider platform
org: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (incl. Fortuneo; Keytrade parent)
vector: Reported entry through an external service provider's platform (bank/press); root cause not disclosed
sequence: Fraudulent transfers to other banks; funds reportedly converted to crypto (on-chain investigators first flagged >USD 106m on 2 Nov); some transfers paused; some funds frozen.
systems: Not disclosed; reportedly a provider platform connected to bank payment flows
stolen_orig: Reported EUR ~100-118m (USD ~106-133m); NOT confirmed by bank
downtime: Some transfers delayed; app issues reported
customers: Bank: no customer losses; customer accounts not accessed
regulatory: Banque de France reportedly notified; Paris prosecutor investigation reported by some outlets (not verified here)
fs_impact: Bank's own funds; group CET1 not disclosed as affected
failed: Transfer monitoring did not prevent outflow
worked: Freezing of some funds; customer protection
lessons: Bank-to-crypto conversion collapses recovery windows; on-chain analysts may detect before the bank discloses.
unresolved: Confirmed amount; entry point; recovered share; actor
verification: web-verified 2026-11-07 (multiple outlets; seed Reuters URL not retrievable - paywall/401)

name: 'CRAFTY FALCON' AI-assisted campaign against Indian financial sector (CERT-In/I4C advisory)
org: NBFCs, digital lenders, fintechs, payment aggregators/PSPs, crypto exchanges
vector: Reported use of publicly available AI-driven offensive tools for vulnerability discovery and rapid exploitation
sequence: Per press: AI-assisted recon/exploitation; re-targeting after incomplete remediation; unauthorized fund transfers via APIs.
regulatory: CERT-In critical advisory; I4C warning (4 Nov 2026)
lessons: Officially-named AI-assisted campaign - but degree of autonomy is unverified.
unresolved: Advisory text not retrieved; victims; amounts; actual role of AI

name: Shinkin Banks West Japan Center outage (NON-CYBERATTACK comparator)
org: 128 shinkin banks (Shinkin Kyodo Center West Japan Center)
sequence: ATMs, counters, online transactions halted at ~3,430 branches; East Japan Center unaffected.
customers: Customers of 128 shinkin banks in western Japan
regulatory: FSA reporting expected
worked: Same-day restoration; regional separation limited scope
lessons: Shared-utility models for small banks concentrate operational risk regardless of cause.
